result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.is_valid_coloring()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Check if a coloring is valid (no adjacent nodes share a color). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L26848-L26901){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.is_valid_coloring(coloring) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Is valid coloring](/assets/graphs/is-valid-coloring.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same two-by-three ladder on both sides, each node filled with its color and badged with the color number. Left: no edge joins two nodes of the same color, so is_valid_coloring() returns True. Right: F is recolored to 2, the same color as its neighbor C, and that edge (shown in the accent color) makes is_valid_coloring() return False." width="100%"} ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [coloring]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[int, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A dictionary mapping node IDs to colors (integers). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the coloring is valid, `False` otherwise. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a path `A-B-C`, alternating colors between neighbors produces a valid coloring: ::: {#8fd3bbc3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) node_ids = graph.get_node_ids() # Valid coloring (alternating colors) valid = {node_ids[0]: 0, node_ids[1]: 1, node_ids[2]: 0} # Returns True graph.is_valid_coloring(valid) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Assigning the same color to two adjacent nodes (`A` and `B`) makes the coloring invalid: ::: {#93d697c5 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Invalid coloring (adjacent nodes share a color) invalid = {node_ids[0]: 0, node_ids[1]: 0, node_ids[2]: 1} # Returns False graph.is_valid_coloring(invalid) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` False ``` ::: :::
